newsitem.title: KUWAIT: KNPC boosts Kuwait refining capacity to 895,000 bp.
newsitem.headline: KNPC boosts Kuwait refining capacity to 895,000 bp.

text.p: State-owned oil refiner Kuwait National Petroleum Co has raised its domestic refining capacity to 895,000 barrels per day, the official Kuwait News Agency reported on Sunday.
"KNPC announced today that the refining capacity at the (Mina) al-Shuaiba refinery was increased to...195,000 bpd," said the agency.
"With this increase the total refining capacity of (local) Kuwaiti refineries rises to 895,000 bpd," it said.
The increase brings Shuaiba's capacity to the pre-Gulf War level from about 160,000 bpd in recent months.
Kuwait's other two domestic refineries, Mina al-Ahmadi and Mina Abdullah, have a refining capacity of 445,000 bpd and 255,000 bpd respectively, it said.

The capacity rise came from repairs at Mina al-Shuaiba. A project to repair an isomax unit at Mina al-Shuaiba, the only remaining war-damaged facility at the refinery, is expected to be concluded at the end of June, it said.
Most of the Gulf state's oil production and refining facilities were damaged during the 1990-91 Iraqi occupation of Kuwait.
KNPC, which runs the three refineries, is the refining arm of the Kuwait Petroleum Corp which oversees the oil sector. OPEC member Kuwait has a crude production quota of 2.0 million bpd.
